input: Apply for a patent for my product idea

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether the idea is a physical product, software, process, or design determines which type of patent to pursue (utility, design, plant, provisional vs. non-provisional).
Whether the user is filing alone, with co-inventors, or through a company affects ownership, assignment, and legal requirements on the application.
The country or region where they want protection determines the filing body (USPTO, EPO, PCT, etc.) and the entire procedural path.
Budget directly determines whether a patent attorney is involved, whether they file provisional first, and which filing tracks are feasible.
Whether they plan to hire a patent attorney/agent or file pro se (self-represented) completely changes the immediate next action and plan complexity.
Understanding the end goal — e.g., stopping competitors, licensing the idea, attracting investors, or selling the patent — shapes how broadly and aggressively to draft claims.
How urgent their timeline is (e.g., public disclosure already made, product launch imminent) affects whether speed or thoroughness should be prioritised.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for a patent for my product idea
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to file a patent application to protect their product idea, but key details about the invention, jurisdiction, experience, and approach are unknown.

questions.title: What type of invention is your product idea?
questions.description: Is it a physical/mechanical product, a software or app, a manufacturing process, an ornamental design, or something else? This determines the correct patent type (utility, design, provisional, etc.).

questions.title: Which country or region must the patent protect?
questions.description: Are you seeking protection in one country (e.g., the US), multiple specific countries, or internationally via a PCT application? This defines the entire filing path and body.

questions.title: Are you the sole inventor, or are others involved?
questions.description: Will this be filed under your name alone, with co-inventors, or assigned to a company or employer? Ownership and inventorship affect the legal requirements of the application.

questions.title: What is your budget for the patent process?
questions.description: Do you have a rough budget in mind — e.g., under $1,000 for a DIY provisional, $5,000–$15,000+ for a full attorney-filed utility patent? Budget is the single biggest constraint on what is feasible.

questions.title: Do you plan to hire a patent attorney or file yourself?
questions.description: Will you engage a registered patent attorney or agent, use an online filing service, or file pro se (on your own)? This determines the immediate first action and plan complexity.

questions.title: What is the main goal of holding this patent?
questions.description: Is the primary aim to block competitors, license the technology, attract investors, or prepare the idea for sale? The end goal shapes how broadly the patent claims should be drafted.

questions.title: How urgent is your filing timeline right now?
questions.description: Have you already publicly disclosed the idea, or is a launch or investor pitch imminent? Urgency determines whether you need a quick provisional filing first or can take time for a thorough non-provisional application.
